tasks.spec: You are solving a reliability problem that three rounds of prompt-tuning have failed to fix. BOUNDARY: read only inside your own task directory; everything you need is staged in ./source/. Never modify anything outside your task directory, never call an API, never send a message. You own exactly one output file: ./report.md. THE SYSTEM: an SMS agent books eye exams for an optometry practice. The patient says when they would like to come in, a step captures that intent into five variables, and those five variables are sent verbatim as the body of a scheduling search. If any variable holds a value the schedule cannot parse, the search fails and the patient's conversation is damaged. THE PROBLEM: capture is done by the platform's variable-extraction feature, which is a small language model given one written description per field. The same patient sentence does not reliably produce the same capture. READ ./source/MEASURED-EVIDENCE.md FIRST. It contains executed measurements, including a table of six identical runs where two produced a broken capture, the exact list of phrases the schedule accepts and rejects, and the fact that unfilled variables arrive as JSON null and are rejected as non-strings. Treat every measurement in it as fact. Also read ./source/v41_graph.json for the live graph, especially the extractVars descriptions on n_negotiate, n_ask and n_reask, and ./source/build_v41.py which generates them. YOUR JOB: work out what would make this capture DETERMINISTIC, or as close to it as this platform allows, and say so concretely. Consider and explicitly weigh at least these options, plus any better one you find: rewriting the field descriptions again and why that keeps failing; reducing the number of captured fields so there are fewer places for a value to land wrongly; capturing one combined free-text field and normalising it downstream where code rather than a model decides; making the receiving end tolerant so that a value the schedule cannot parse is corrected rather than rejected; and using a constrained enumeration where the model picks from a fixed list instead of writing free text. For each option state what it costs, what it cannot fix, and how it would be proven. Then commit to ONE recommendation and defend it. OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md: start with '# Extraction Reliability'. Include '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, then '## Findings', then '## Clean', then '## Assumptions'. Each finding uses exactly: '### Finding: <one line>' then 'Evidence:' citing the specific node id, field name or measurement, 'Impact:' in terms of what a patient experiences, 'Fix:' concrete enough to implement, 'Priority: P0|P1|P2|P3', 'Confidence: high|medium|low'. Cite real node ids from the graph. End with a section '## Recommendation' naming the single option you would implement and the executable test that would prove it worked. HARD RULES: never invent a node id or a field name; never contradict a measurement in the evidence file without your own measurement, which you cannot take, so treat them as fixed; put anything unverifiable under Assumptions. Under 1500 words.
tasks.verified: report.md has all sections, cites at least 4 real node ids, invents none, every finding carries evidence, impact, fix, priority and confidence

tasks.spec: You are designing a fix that cannot be done where everyone keeps trying to do it. BOUNDARY: read only inside your own task directory; everything you need is staged in ./source/. Never modify anything outside your task directory, never call an API, never send a message. You own exactly one output file: ./report.md. THE PROBLEM: patients of an optometry practice receive appointment offers that read '07/27/2026 11:30 am', a first name in raw capitals as the practice system stores it, and an internal location code. It should read as a weekday and time a person recognises, a normally capitalised name, and a place name. READ ./source/MEASURED-EVIDENCE.md FIRST for the executed measurements, including the exact response shape the scheduling gateway returns and the proof that this cannot be fixed in a prompt. The platform substitutes an interpolated variable directly into the outgoing message, so the model never gets an opportunity to reformat it; this was proven three separate times. Also read ./source/v41_graph.json to see exactly where these values are interpolated, in particular the message templates on n_ask and n_offer and the responseData mappings on the webhook nodes. YOUR JOB: design the change to the gateway response that fixes this, precisely enough that someone could implement it without asking you a question. Decide and justify: whether to add new display fields alongside the raw ones or to change the existing fields, and what that choice means for the other practice already consuming this same endpoint, which must not break; exactly what the new field names and value formats should be, with worked examples for a same-week appointment and one further out; where the timezone comes from and why, given that a related endpoint already returns clinic-local times mislabelled with a UTC suffix; how a name in raw capitals should be normalised, including the cases that naive title-casing gets wrong; and what the pathway then has to change to consume it. Include an explicit backward-compatibility argument, and the executable test that proves the change works. OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md: start with '# Display Formatting Design'. Include '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, then '## Findings', then '## Clean', then '## Assumptions'. Each finding uses exactly: '### Finding: <one line>' then 'Evidence:' citing a node id or the measured response shape, 'Impact:' in patient terms, 'Fix:' concrete, 'Priority: P0|P1|P2|P3', 'Confidence: high|medium|low'. Cite real node ids. End with '## Proposed Contract' giving the exact JSON the gateway should return. HARD RULES: never invent a node id or a response field that is not in the evidence; do not propose a prompt-only fix, it is proven not to work; put anything unverifiable under Assumptions. Under 1500 words.
tasks.verified: report.md has all sections, cites at least 4 real node ids, proposes a gateway-side contract rather than a prompt change, every finding carries the required fields

tasks.spec: You are auditing a test suite, not the system it tests. BOUNDARY: read only inside your own task directory; everything is staged in ./source/. Never modify anything outside your task directory, never call an API, never run the suite. You own exactly one output file: ./report.md. WHAT YOU ARE AUDITING: ./source/scenarios.py holds 30 QA cases for an SMS appointment-booking agent, and ./source/pathway_harness.py is the runner that executes them. ./source/v41_graph.json is the conversation graph they test, for checking that a case aims somewhere real. WHY THIS MATTERS: four cases in this very suite have already been found to FAIL CORRECT BEHAVIOUR because they asserted on particular wording rather than on substance. One rejected 'I have not booked you for anything yet' as a booking claim, because the pattern matched the words inside the denial. Another rejected 'we do not have any openings at 3am' as though the agent had offered 3am. A suite that fails correct behaviour is worse than no suite, because it trains everyone to ignore red. YOUR JOB: find every remaining case that could fail correct behaviour, and every case that could PASS incorrect behaviour, which is the more dangerous direction. For each case ask: does the assertion test what must be TRUE, or merely how it happened to be phrased? Could the agent do the right thing in different words and still fail? Could the agent do something harmful and still pass? Is expect_node the real requirement, or would several nodes be acceptable? Does a regex account for negation, casing, and punctuation? Is any case's 'why' actually describing something different from what the case asserts? Are there gaps: an important behaviour with no case at all? Pay particular attention to any case that asserts on a single node id when the graph shows a global node with auto-return, because such a conversation legitimately ends up back where it started. OUTPUT CONTRACT for ./report.md: start with '# Suite Audit'. Include '## Summary' with at most 3 bullets, then '## Findings', then '## Clean', then '## Assumptions'. Each finding uses exactly: '### Finding: <one line>' then 'Evidence:' naming the scenario by its exact name and quoting the assertion, 'Impact:' saying whether it risks failing correct behaviour or passing incorrect behaviour, 'Fix:' giving the replacement assertion, 'Priority: P0|P1|P2|P3', 'Confidence: high|medium|low'. Cite real node ids from the graph where relevant. HARD RULES: never invent a scenario name or a node id; quote assertions exactly as written; put anything uncertain under Assumptions. Under 1400 words.
tasks.verified: report.md has all sections, cites at least 4 real node ids, names scenarios that genuinely exist, and every finding carries evidence, impact, fix, priority and confidence
